label: Last original tokens and <DEL> of long (L>=8) sequences, content-gated
explanation: Fires only at absolute steps 5-9, in the input phase or on <DEL>; never in the copy phase and never at t<=4. 98% of activation mass is at t=6-9, mostly the final 1-2 original tokens and the <DEL> step of L=8/9 sequences (L=9 holds 67% of mass, L<=6 almost none). The rate climbs with orig_idx (3% at idx 6, 13% at idx 7, 24% at idx 8), so it acts like a late-position / near-end-of-input detector. Within that window it is sparse and depends on sequence content in a diffuse way: it fires more when the first token is a/r/p/j/b/k/i/o (about 2.6x for a/r/p), when there are more digits among the originals (rate rises steadily with n_digits), and on first occurrences of the input token. No single content rule captures this, so precision stays low (about 12%). The predicate covers about 88% of activation mass. The strongest examples have digits early in the sequence (e.g. b 3 2 2 r 2 ...), with the peak on the last original token, which is often b.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig2=3 (+3.37), orig1=3 (+3.16), orig2=2 (+3.11), orig1=r (+3.01), orig1=p (+2.95), orig1=o (+2.83). Lower it: phase=2 (-10.67), prev3_tok=- (-7.62), t=3 (-6.74), t=4 (-6.73).
